subject: zoology
question_text: What is Aristotle's lantern? Give one example of an animal possessing it.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.53, VSAQ 96). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it is
steps.why: The apparatus is named by its jaw count, so five jaws is the fact that carries the mark.
common_mistakes: Giving the number of jaws as three. Three jaws belong to the pedicellariae; the lantern has five.
Writing that it lies in the stomach. It lies in the buccal cavity, at the mouth.
steps.memory_tip: Five jaws matches the five-part symmetry of the echinoderm body.
steps.margin_note: Say what it is, how many jaws it has, and where it lies.
lines: apparatus in the buccal cavity of a sea
It is made of five calcareous jaws, each
carrying one tooth, held together by muscles
The five teeth meet at the mouth and scrape

steps.label: One example
steps.why: The lantern is present only in the urchins that scrape hard surfaces, which is why the burrowing heart urchin and sand dollar do without it.
common_mistakes: Naming a starfish. The lantern belongs to the sea urchins, class Echinoidea.
Writing that every echinoid has one. The heart urchin and the sand dollar do not.
steps.memory_tip: Lantern goes with Echinoidea, and Echinus is the named example.
steps.margin_note: One example is asked for. Add the two echinoids that lack it if there is room.
lines: It is present in sea urchins.
It is absent in the heart urchin

insider_note: The examiner is looking for two words, five-jawed and sea urchin; the name Echinus alone has earned the second mark.
